All set · Keyguard is ready to use

To warn you as you type, Keyguard reads the text you type on its own keyboard.

What happens to it:

• Checking happens on this device, using a built-in list of patterns. No network is involved.
• Nothing you type is saved. Text is held in memory only while you're typing and is discarded when you switch fields.
• Password fields are never checked. Detection and network activity are switched off completely for them.
• Nothing you type is ever written to logs or crash reports.

Keyguard can only see what you type on its own keyboard. It cannot read messages you receive, and it cannot see what you type on any other keyboard.

Double-checking (optional, off by default) is the one exception. If you turn it on, a flagged phrase and up to a few recent messages are sent to a server to be reviewed by an AI — this is what tells “I want to die of embarrassment” apart from something serious. Even then, your full typing is never sent, and nothing is sent from password fields. You can turn it off at any time.

A parent can always see:

• The kind of warning you got, and how serious it was
• Whether you deleted the message or sent it anyway
• The time it happened

They can never see:

• Who you were talking to, or which app you were using
• Anything you type in a password field
• Messages you receive

How much else they can see is a setting they choose. The line below says which one is switched on right now, and it will change here if they change it.

Warnings about hurting yourself are included in what they see.

They can also change how forceful warnings are, whether you are able to dismiss a warning at all, and whether double-checking is switched on.

Warns before you send something risky

Keyguard reads the text you are typing so it can warn you before you send personal information, or something that could hurt you or someone else. It never reads password fields. It does not record which app you are using. If this device is supervised, what a parent can see is listed on the Keyguard setup screen.
Keyguard now works on top of the keyboard you already use, so typing stays exactly as smooth as it is today. It needs two permissions to do that.
Allow Keyguard to see what you type
In the list that opens, find “Keyguard safety warnings” and turn it on.
Without this, Keyguard could watch your typing and have no way to warn you. It will not run until this is on.

Let Keyguard see what you type

Keyguard works on top of the keyboard you already use, so typing stays exactly as it is. To warn you, it needs to see the text as you write it. It never looks at password fields, and it does not record which app you are in.
In the list that opens, find “Keyguard safety warnings” and turn it on.

One more. Keyguard needs permission to draw over other apps so the warning can appear above your keyboard.
Without it Keyguard would be able to see what you type and have no way to warn you, so it will not run until this is on.
